a_raw: {"translation": "Target defines the following proposition (it names a Prop without asserting or proving it): For all types X and Y, and for every finite-component synchronous state machine N with inputs in X and outputs in Y — where such a machine consists of a finite type of components A1, a state type A3(n) for each component n in A1 (not required to be finite), an initial global state assigning an element of A3(n) to each n, a synchronous update rule a5(n, σ, x) giving the next state of component n from the current global state σ and an input x in X, and an output map a6 from global states to Y — there exists another such machine N' (with the same input type X and output type Y) satisfying all three of the following conditions: (1) N' has exactly one component, i.e., the cardinality of its component type A1 is 1 (with no restriction on the state type of that single component); (2) for every pair of distinct components m ≠ n of N', it is not the case that there is both a nonempty directed path (one or more steps) from m to n and a nonempty directed path from n to m in N''s dependency graph, where there is a directed edge from m to n iff there exist two global states σ and σ' agreeing on every component k ≠ m and an input x in X such that component n's update differs on (σ, x) and (σ', x); and (3) for every finite list xs of inputs in X (of any length, including the empty list), N' and N produce the exact same output in Y when each starts from its initial global state, synchronously updates all components left-to-right for each input in xs, and applies its output map to the resulting global state. Note that condition (2) only rules out mutual reachability between distinct components — it does not forbid a component from depending on itself (self-loops) — and because condition (1) forces N' to have only one component, there are no distinct pairs m ≠ n, so condition (2) holds vacuously."}

divergences.description: While the claim highlights that the degenerate single-unit construction works 'if a unit may have memory, as Hanson and Walker's flip-flops do', the Lean model S1 relies on more than allowing self-loops (permitted by D12): it also leaves each unit's state type A3 n completely unconstrained, allowing a single unit to hold the entire global state of N rather than a bounded elementary state space like a flip-flop. Given the author's explicit framing as a degenerate case and disclaimer regarding simple Krohn-Rhodes components, this is a minor caveat.

The source passage concerns finite-state automata (FSA), whereas S1 only requires finitely many units (Fintype A1) and imposes no finiteness constraint on the input type X, output type Y, or per-unit state types A3 n; Target also does not explicitly assert that N' has a finite state space when N does.

The source passage speaks of realizing an FSA isomorphically, whereas S1 models deterministic Moore machines with a distinguished initial state a4 and S1.D6 only asserts input-output equivalence from that initial state across all finite input sequences (which matches the claim's 'same behaviour at every horizon', though it is weaker than automaton isomorphism).

judgement.summary: Target faithfully formalizes the author's claimed degenerate case: every finite-component synchronous machine has a single-unit behavioural twin with no feedback between distinct units (vacuously satisfying D12) and identical outputs on all finite input sequences. The only divergences relative to the passage and claim are minor modeling idealizations: unconstrained (potentially infinite) state/input/output types, reliance on arbitrary per-unit state size in addition to memory, and behavioural equivalence from a fixed initial state rather than isomorphism.
